entry.title: Add rel notes and experimental features notes for fx speculation rule…
entry.content:
…s support

Description

Firefox 155 enabled support for a limited subset of speculation rules functionality, in Nightly only. From looking at https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2041381#c11, it appears that

  • only prefetch is supported (not prerender)
  • with immediate eagerness only
  • and only a urls list, which means that the source value of list is also supported.

Firefox 158 added the moderate eagerness value; see https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2061013.

This PR adds rel notes and experimental feature notes for all this stuff.

Motivation

entry.title: fix(js): correct expected output of four JavaScript examples
entry.content:
Four JavaScript examples document an expected output that the code in the same code block cannot produce. I ran each block with Node 24 (browsers agree for these cases) to check.

Date.prototype.setSeconds() — files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/date/setseconds/index.md

const event = new Date("August 19, 1975 23:15:30");
event.setSeconds(42);
console.log(event);
// Expected output: "Sat Apr 19 1975 23:15:42 GMT+0100 (CET)"   <- says April

setSeconds() does not change the month. August 19, 1975 is a Tuesday, so the line becomes:

Tue Aug 19 1975 23:15:42 GMT+0100 (CET)

handler.construct() — files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/proxy/proxy/construct/index.md

The trap logs Creating a ${target.name} and the target is the function Monster, so the console shows Creating a Monster — the existing // Expected output: "Creating a monster" has the wrong case.

String.prototype.toLocaleLowerCase() — files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/string/tolocalelowercase/index.md

Both logged values are template literals that add a prefix, so the expected output of the first line is "EN-US: i̇stanbul" (not "i̇stanbul") and of the second one "TR: istanbul" (not "istanbul").

Promise() — files/en-us/web/javascript/reference/global_objects/promise/promise/index.md

console.log(promise1);
// Expected output: [object Promise]

[object Promise] is the result of String(promise1) (or Object.prototype.toString.call(promise1)); console.log prints the promise object itself, which consoles render as Promise {<pending>} (Chrome) or Promise { <state>: "pending" } (Firefox). I used the latter, the form already used on Promise.all().

Checks: node scripts/front-matter_linter.js, npx markdownlint-cli2, npx prettier -c, npx cspell --config .vscode/cspell.json and npm test — all pass.

entry.title: Update persistent/non-persistent notifications docs
entry.content:
This is basically #41267, rebased on the current docs.

Since I made #41267, the notifications docs have acknowledged the difference between persistent and non-persistent notifications, but I thought there was still some clarity that could be added, and some errors still (e.g. persistent notifications are not only created from a SW, they can also be created by a web page).

One thing I wasn't sure about was whether click, close, and show are only fired on NP notifications.

Coming back to this PR, I remember why I stalled last time: the guide page https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notifications_API/Using_the_Notifications_API needs a complete rewrite with new examples. I think the to-do list example is much too complex - I shouldn't have to understand IndexedDB to understand notifications.

I'm not proposing to do that in this PR, in the interests of finally getting it merged. But we need to do it.

entry.title: build(filecheck): replace imagemin with sharp
entry.content:
Description

Update filecheck to compress JPEG, PNG, and GIF images with sharp and optimize SVGs with SVGO directly. Remove imagemin dependencies and temporary compression files.

Motivation

Simplify image compression dependencies and remove standalone binary installation scripts.

Additional details

Regression tests cover format preservation, GIF frames and timing, transparency, EXIF orientation, and file size limits.

Behavior changes compared to imagemin:

  • JPEG: mozjpeg's cjpeg reused the quality of JPEG input and kept its metadata, so it never flagged a JPEG in this repo. sharp re-encodes at quality 75 with mozjpeg optimizations and applies the EXIF orientation before stripping metadata. A full run over files/ newly flags 15 existing files (13 JPEGs, 1 PNG, 1 GIF), which CI only reports once a PR touches them.
  • GIF: gifsicle was lossless. sharp re-quantizes frames: 55 of the 58 GIFs in this repo re-encode pixel-identical, the other 3 show small colour shifts or merge a near-duplicate frame while keeping its delay, and none of them exceeds the compression threshold.
